revision_focus: The principal lexical candidates now have formal correspondence audits in addition to source-independence controls. Six priority families reach grade A; blue-green remains A- pending historical-root mapping.

historical_core.steffel: ameke is source-explicit participial; final ke is often omitted in pronunciation; short -ame forms are source-attested
historical_core.merrill: relevant historical chains are analyzed with participial -(a)me plus optional reduplicative -kV/-ke; Merrill is an analytical layer on Steffel, not a second historical lexical witness

modern_core.caballero_2022: independent Choguita grammar documents participial -ame/-kame and provides lexical/morphological controls such as kotʃi and siˈríame
modern_core.compendio_1997: independent multivariety source documents -kame/-kami/-name/-nami/-ame/-ami/-m in color morphology and explicitly labels -ame participial
modern_core.sep_community_2010: independent bilingual community texts provide nise’ami in the shepherd domain and chiperami in a board-like/flat context
modern_core.src02: rich internal modern documentary layer, but bibliographic identity remains unresolved and likely tied to a pre-2016 Hilton lineage; it is not counted as independent from Hilton where exact overlaps occur

formal_controls_now_established.historical_ss: Merrill normalizes intervocalic Steffel <ss> to [s], eliminating a false gemination problem in Nessé~Nisé
formal_controls_now_established.historical_e_i: Merrill documents e~i variation elsewhere in Steffel
formal_controls_now_established.modern_pretonic_e_i: Caballero documents optional pretonic/posttonic /e/ raising to [i]
formal_controls_now_established.historical_tsch: Merrill identifies Steffel <tsch> as the voiceless palatoalveolar affricate [č] and provides phonetic normalizations
formal_controls_now_established.historical_l_r: Steffel/Merrill document l~r alternation; cavólameke~cavórameke provides a same-domain control
formal_controls_now_established.ameke_ame: Steffel's ke-omission statement, Merrill's -(a)me+-ke analysis and modern productive -ame provide independent constructional controls

candidate_ranking_v5.strongest_point: lexical sleep family and participial function independently align historically and in modern Choguita/SRC-02
historical nesé and modern nisé align in stress/semantics; apparent ss problem disappears; e~i has historical and modern controls; independent Balleza shepherd usage
candidate_ranking_v5.open_problem: direction, geography and chronology of e~i; publication-level cognacy not yet adjudicated

candidate_ranking_v5.strongest_point: historical čipér- and modern chipér-/chiper- align in affricate, stress and flat/thin semantics; correspondence is controlled by other families and an independent Guerrero token
candidate_ranking_v5.open_problem: lexeme-specific history of -ameke~-ami and explicit bare-stem analysis

candidate_ranking_v5.strongest_point: explicit historical govern->governor pair plus independent Choguita governor form; e~i, l~r and -ameke~-ame all have external controls
candidate_ranking_v5.open_problem: competing cultural-historical etymology selígame ‘spear bearer’ < selaka ‘spear’ must be traced and reconciled

candidate_ranking_v5.strongest_point: published historical-modern comparison plus independent multivariety chó- morphology
candidate_ranking_v5.open_problem: history/order of k-material and exact relationship among surface participial complexes

candidate_ranking_v5.strongest_point: multiple published historical forms and independent multivariety rosá- morphology
modern seyó/siyó paradigms are strongly replicated across varieties and published comparisons connect them to Steffel blue/green forms
candidate_ranking_v5.open_problem: formal mapping of multiple historical Steffel roots to modern seyó/siyó has not yet been resolved

model_v5.preferred: continuity of an ame-centered participial/derivational domain, combined with variety-specific additional morphology, phonology, stem structure and lexicalization
model_v5.new_bottleneck: candidate-specific historical reconstruction rather than discovery of more unfiltered string matches or source-independent modern tokens

publication_level_claim_v5: After controlling documentary dependence and formally auditing several candidate-specific correspondences, six priority families now combine historical source evidence, independent modern Rarámuri support and external controls for their main formal differences. This materially strengthens an ame-centered participial/derivational continuity hypothesis. The next publication-level task is not to multiply matches but to reconstruct candidate-specific sound correspondences, stem histories and competing etymologies, beginning with blue-green mapping and the unresolved -mé/selígame problems.
methodological_rules: Every substantive research step is logged in Notion with method, result, cautions, artifacts/commits and next action.
Grades measure evidential architecture, not cognacy probability.
Critical editions/analyses do not count as new lexical attestations of the same source material.
Potentially dependent Hilton/SRC-02 overlaps do not count as independent replication.
Candidate-specific formal differences must be controlled using evidence outside the target word.
Competing etymologies are preserved rather than silently reconciled.
Superseded versions remain in the repository for auditability.
